doc.title: Bob Cranshaw interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

title: Meeting Sonny Rollins and getting the Playboy Jazz Festival job
summary: Playing as a package with Walter Perkins at the London House, Cranshaw was hired when Sonny Rollins asked Perkins to choose a bassist for the first Playboy Jazz Festival.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: That’s marvelous. And of course we’re filming this at our college, and I’m glad that students are hearing this, that it takes a combination of those skills. Tell us when you first started working with Sonny Rollins.

I worked with Sonny, starting I think in 1959 or ‘60. Sonny — I played the first Playboy Jazz Festival. And I met Sonny before around Chicago, but I never worked with Sonny, usually Victor Sproles or different bass players who were a little older usually worked with Sonny, and who were more established. And one day Sonny heard Walter Perkins the drummer and I, who, we came as a package you know. We worked a lot of jobs at the London House and different places on the off nights for Oscar Peterson, and people like that, we would work opposite them one night and spell another band that was there on Mondays and Tuesdays. So I got a chance to meet a lot of the name people and play opposite them. But it gave me a chance to meet a lot of people. And through this one day Sonny was doing the Playboy Festival, and he asked Walter Perkins to do it and he said, “Walter, get the bass player who you would like.” So I was hired.
